request: Imagine the black handle is a stand. Add another one on the other side of device in approximately same distane from side wall as the existing one. Remove the Cordholder. Cut the bottom of the handles so it allows the device to be stable on a flat surface.

actions.operation: Create another handle based on the existing black handle.

parameters.offset: approximately the same distance from the side wall as the existing handle

actions.target: the existing black handle and the other side of the device
actions.relational_constraint: Place the new handle on the opposite side of the device, at approximately the same side-wall distance as the existing handle.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the existing black handle, the corresponding opposite side of the device, the applicable side wall, and the existing handle-to-side-wall distance.
steps: Identify the black handle in the multiview images as the external U-shaped support cradle in section R04, principally feature F020. Its outer and inner curved strap surfaces are FACE 365 and FACE 366, and its two planar thickness faces are FACE 368 at CAD y=304.80001 and FACE 370 at CAD y=279.400009.
Use the principal housing end faces to define the longitudinal placement references. FACE 45 is the housing end interface at CAD y=355.6, while FACE 46 is the opposite housing end wall at CAD y=0.

Determine the existing cradle clearance from the adjacent high-CAD-Y housing end. The nearest cradle side is FACE 368 at y=304.80001, giving an end-wall distance of approximately 355.6 - 304.80001 = 50.8 mm.
Create a datum plane at the longitudinal midpoint of the housing, CAD y=177.8, halfway between FACE 45 and FACE 46.

Duplicate the complete cradle geometry, including F020 and its paired pin-interface features F021 and F022. Preserve the U-shaped strap profile, 25.400001 mm longitudinal thickness, and the radius-7.62 mm pin bores represented by FACE 361 and FACE 362.
Mirror the duplicate across the datum plane at y=177.8. Equivalently, transform its longitudinal coordinates using y_new = 355.6 - y_original.

The mirrored cradle must span approximately CAD y=50.8 to y=76.2. This leaves approximately 50.8 mm between the new cradle and the opposite housing end wall FACE 46, matching the existing cradle-to-FACE-45 clearance.

Retain the duplicated cradle as a separate assembly solid unless the original cradle is modeled as fused to the housing. Do not merge it with the housing shell if doing so would eliminate the pin or pivot interfaces.
Verify in the +X and -X side views that one cradle is positioned near each longitudinal end of the device and that the two cradle centers are symmetric about y=177.8.
Verify that the new cradle does not intersect the housing, closure assembly, internal mechanism, existing feet, electrical lead, or plug.

actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the feature or body named or functioning as the Cordholder.
steps: Localize the Cordholder using the iso1 and +Y views. The small black U-shaped bracket inside the access opening corresponds most closely to the narrow U-shaped internal support bracket F017 in section R03.

Confirm the candidate by selecting its mirrored side walls FACE 297 at CAD x=-10.16 and FACE 307 at CAD x=10.16. The connected secondary bracket walls and transitions are contained in FACE 298 through FACE 310.
Select the complete connected body or source feature that generates F017 rather than deleting only FACE 297 and FACE 307.

Suppress or delete the Cordholder body/feature and all of its connected bracket faces. If the imported STEP topology does not preserve a separate feature history, identify the connected solid owning the F017 faces and remove that solid from the assembly.
Do not remove neighboring cylindrical reel surfaces or shaft geometry belonging to F014, F015, F016, F018, or F019.
Recompute the assembly and verify through the access opening that the small U-shaped Cordholder is absent and that no residual disconnected bracket faces remain.

actions.operation: Cut or trim the bottom of both handles.
actions.target: the bottoms of the existing handle and the newly added handle
actions.relational_constraint: The resulting handle bottoms must allow the device to rest stably on a flat surface.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify both handles, their bottom regions, the required cut extent, and the flat support plane needed for stable placement.
steps: Use the existing standing feet as the authoritative flat-support reference. FACE 332 on F023 and FACE 351 on F024 are coplanar ground seats at CAD z=-142.861301.

Create a datum support plane coincident with FACE 332 and FACE 351 at z=-142.861301. This plane represents the requested flat surface and is more reliable than interpreting the word bottom from a camera label.

Inspect the original cradle F020. Its outer curved surface FACE 365 extends to approximately CAD z=-152.398401, below the foot support plane, so the lower cradle material must be trimmed by approximately 9.54 mm at its deepest point.

Create a cutting half-space or oversized rectangular cutting solid occupying all material below z=-142.861301. Extend the cutter beyond the full X and Y extents of both the original and mirrored cradles.
Boolean-cut the original cradle F020 with the half-space, removing only cradle material for which z is less than -142.861301. Preserve its arms, pin bores F021 and F022, and attachment regions.
Apply the identical Boolean cut to the newly mirrored cradle so both handle-stands terminate at exactly the same support elevation.
The cuts through the curved strap geometry must generate planar seating faces on both cradles, with normals parallel to CAD Z and with all seating points coplanar with FACE 332 and FACE 351.

Keep the new seating faces flat. Do not add a bottom fillet or chamfer that would reduce the intended contact area or shift the lowest point below the support plane. Small edge breaks may be added only to non-contact perimeter edges if required for manufacture.
Check that the two trimmed cradle seats and the existing foot seats do not produce rocking. All intended ground-contact faces must be coincident with z=-142.861301 within the model tolerance.
Verify in the +X and -X side views that neither cradle projects below the feet and that both cradle bottoms present horizontal flat contacts.

Perform an interference and stability check after regeneration. Confirm that the device can rest on the common plane without contact from the housing, cable, plug, or any remaining curved portion of either cradle.

intention: Use the black handle and its added counterpart as stands.
Allow the device to rest stably on a flat surface.
